newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Police continue arrests in East Timor after killing.
newsitem.headline: Police continue arrests in East Timor after killing.

text.p: Indonesian police said on Monday the number of people detained in a continuing sweep against pre-Christmas violence in the former Portuguese colony of East Timor had risen to 12.
East Timor deputy police chief Colonel Atok Rismanto said police investigations had been routine, despite reports of deaths and shootings during the operation.
"There have been 12 people detained, with 10 of them from Dili," Rismanto said.
"There was no-one killed. No-one was shot. If somebody was shot, there would be an uproar and we'd have to make a report," he told Reuters by telephone from Dili.

Last Tuesday an off-duty corporal was beaten to death in the grounds of Dili's cathedral and in other incidents a number of police and soldiers attacked by sections of a crowd of tens of thousands at Dili's airport.

The crowd had gathered to welcome home Nobel Peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo from a trip to Europe where he received his prize in Norway. Belo has publicly apologised for the death of the soldier, a native East Timorese and father of seven.
Residents said that on Saturday night police could be heard operating in Dili's eastern suburbs of Becora and Coluhon, but added they did not have confirmed reports of any recent shootings.

On Monday, the official Antara news agency reported that East Timor's police chief Colonel Yusuf Muharam had said police were looking for another 18 "witnesses" in relation to last week's attacks, which included the beating of Dili's police chief.

East Timor was invaded by Indonesia in December 1975 and declared its 27th province the following year in an act not recognised by the United Nations. It regards Portugal as being the territory's administering power.
